rules.title: Borrow sequences, bound generated code
rules.what: Take openArray, var or lent parameters instead of copying seqs, reserve with newSeqOfCap, and keep macro and static generation bounded.
rules.why: A seq passed by value is copied; macros and static blocks can generate more code than anyone reads, slowing every build and shipping in every binary.
rules.how: proc f(xs: openArray[int]); newSeqOfCap[int](n); prefer a template where a macro is not needed; inspect expanded code when build size grows.

patterns.note: seq parameter by value; openArray or var avoids the copy.

verify.how: Build time and binary size tracked; allocation profile on hot procs.

rules.title: Deterministic cleanup, chosen memory strategy
rules.what: Close files and sockets with defer or try/finally on every exit path, and choose ARC/ORC and allocation strategies from measured latency and memory needs.
rules.why: A resource closed only at the end of a proc leaks when an exception leaves early, exactly when the system is struggling.
rules.how: let f = open(path); defer: f.close(); --mm:orc by default, measured alternatives for latency-sensitive code.

patterns.note: Resource opened in a file with no defer/finally.

verify.how: Failure-path test shows the resource closed; memory strategy documented with its measurement.
